tasks.short: Develop environmental education programmes and curricula for schools.

steps.what: Establish schools' educational needs and practical programme constraints
Select environmental evidence and suitable learning experiences
Design the environmental curriculum objectives and activity sequence
Write curriculum explanations, activity instructions and teacher notes

loop.purpose: Draft age-appropriate educational prose from the naturalist's outline.
loop.input: Selected source passages, age group, objectives and activity sequence.
loop.output: Draft explanations and instructions with source links and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Naturalist checks factual accuracy, age suitability and whether instructions describe the intended activity.
loop.stop: One revision; unsuitable or unsupported passages are written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template gives structure but does not adapt varied explanations to the chosen audience.

steps.what: Lay out the curriculum in the programme document template
Check and revise environmental curriculum content, accessibility and field practicality

tasks.design: Start with a reusable curriculum structure in {DOCS}; use a bounded loop for source-based explanations and a native template for layout. The naturalist chooses objectives and activities, checks prose and revises the final curriculum.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explanations, instructions and document layout are repeatedly prepared for different school groups.
tasks.enabler_now: Selected evidence and explicit objectives can constrain drafting, while native templates handle layout.
tasks.still_hard: An attractive activity can still be unsafe, inaccessible or educationally weak.
tasks.human_edge: Choose authentic learning experiences and judge what a school group can do in the park.

ambition.what: Adapt a checked programme for another age group with fresh suitability checks.

tasks.altitude: Spend preparation time on educational choices and field practicality.

reach.task: Connect park activities to classroom learning
reach.learn: Specify prior knowledge, accessibility needs and intended learning outcomes.

evidence.claim: Source-bounded drafting and native curriculum layout could reduce writing and formatting; this programme-development saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Needs discussion, evidence selection, curriculum design, prose writing, layout and revision are all priced. The task develops material; no distribution action is proposed.

The naturalist produces age group and constraints in s1, identified source passages in s2 and objectives, activities and sequence in s3. Their full time includes capture. Missing support stops drafting for manual completion in s4.
The s4 naturalist produces checked draft content for the s5 formatter; missing headings or invalid activity references return to manual editing in s6.
Use native structure and layout first. No separate savings or approval gate are claimed for the author's internal save.
unknowns: Actual proportion of writing and layout in current curriculum development.
research_questions: Does a source-based draft reduce total preparation after checks for accuracy, accessibility and field practicality?

already_counted.description: Review and correct drafted curriculum prose.

incremental.description: Maintain source modules and test drafting and layout quality.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=75, gross=25; upkeep=5 gives central net=20. Range allows substantial suitability checking.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with park staff and record agreed programme subjects and schedules.

steps.what: Look up park programme commitments and staff availability
Confer with park staff to determine programme subjects and schedules
Write the agreed park programme schedule and subject record
Send the final programme schedule to park colleagues

tasks.design: Configure a native planning view in {CALENDAR} and a programme schedule template in {DOCS}. Keep the discussion human, then separately record the agreement and send the final schedule through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability lookups and repeated schedule entry surround the planning discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendar views and reusable programme fields reduce clerical preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Staff knowledge, visitor needs and practical park constraints must be reconciled.
tasks.human_edge: Reach a workable agreement about subjects, staffing and timing.
tasks.altitude: Make agreed programmes visible without replacing staff discussion.

reach.learn: Keep resource constraints and agreed dates current.

evidence.claim: Native calendar views and schedule templates could reduce lookup and repeated writing; the saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: The programme record is part of the task and is not folded into the discussion. Sending the agreement is separately counted.
The naturalist produces subject, date, time, location and responsible staff in s3, with 14 retained hours including capture. Missing agreement stays unresolved and is manually clarified before s4.
Try native calendar views and templates first; no automated scheduling or notification is proposed.
The internal record has no self-approval gate; s4 checks the final version and recipients at the real send.
unknowns: Whether programme schedules already use shared native fields.
research_questions: Does the planning view and template reduce lookup and entry while preserving staff agreement?

incremental.description: Maintain planning views and programme fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact programme schedule and colleague distribution list; changes require another send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=92, gross=8; upkeep=2 gives central net=6. Discussion time is fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform park emergency duties, communicate with responders and record the incident.

steps.what: Assess the emergency threat to people, property and natural features
Call emergency responders with the location and observed hazards
Perform immediate emergency protection, first aid or rescue assistance
Hand over observed emergency facts and actions to responders
Write the emergency incident record and outstanding concerns

tasks.design: Retain immediate emergency assessment, response and responder communication with the trained naturalist. A native incident template in {DOCS} reduces repeated record headings after the response.
tasks.previous_blocker: The post-response incident record repeats context fields and standard headings.
tasks.enabler_now: A reusable native incident template can structure the account without directing emergency action.
tasks.still_hard: Rapidly changing hazards and incomplete information require trained human response.
tasks.human_edge: Act within training, notice danger and communicate observations accurately.
tasks.altitude: Preserve emergency response capacity and improve the incident account.

reach.learn: Distinguish observed facts, actions and outstanding concerns.

evidence.claim: A native incident template could remove a small amount of repeated record preparation; it does not automate emergency response and the saving is unmeasured.

assumptions: The emergency record is included as its own step; no emergency field time is reduced.

The naturalist produces incident date, location, observed hazards, assistance, responder handover and outstanding concerns in s5. Eight retained hours include capture and checks. Unknown facts remain unknown; no structured input is fabricated.
The send-time and handover checks in s2 and s4 are immediate checks of what is communicated, not new prior approval that delays emergency action.
Use the existing incident form first; if it already supplies the structure, the record saving is zero. No machine action is proposed.
unknowns: Whether current incident forms already remove all repetitive preparation.
research_questions: Does a native template save any record time once complete and accurate incident writing is counted?

already_counted.description: Write and check the incident record.

approvals.approved_version: Exact emergency location, observed hazards and assistance request spoken to responders; updated information is checked as communicated.
Exact observed facts and actions handed over; distinguish uncertainty before communicating it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 small-record scenario: B=100, R=98, gross=2; upkeep=1 gives central net=1. Existing incident forms could leave zero gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Survey forest conditions and record and assess park flora and fauna.

steps.what: Choose survey routes, sampling methods and reference material
Travel the park survey route and access observation sites
Survey forest conditions and identify and count fauna and flora
Record survey locations, conditions, species, counts and observation effort
Summarise surveyed distribution, abundance and forest condition observations
Determine forest conditions and document distribution and abundance conclusions

tasks.design: Use native survey capture fields and tested summaries in {SPREADSHEET}, with the assessment written in {DOCS}. The naturalist conducts the survey and distinguishes observed abundance from conclusions limited by sampling effort.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated recording structure and manual survey summaries consume time after field observation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable capture fields and formulas can preserve locations, effort and uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Detectability and uncertain identification complicate comparisons across routes and dates.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise species and judge what the survey can establish about the park.

ambition.what: Compare another survey period where methods and effort are compatible.

tasks.altitude: Keep survey conclusions traceable to observations and effort.

reach.learn: Record uncertain identification and observation effort rather than assuming absence.

evidence.claim: Native survey fields and tested summaries could reduce repeated clerical preparation; the park-survey saving is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Routes, travel, observation, the survey record, summaries and written conclusions are counted separately.

The naturalist produces route or location, date, species or uncertainty code, count, condition category, method and effort in s4. Its retained 10.5 hours include capture and checks; s1 defines summaries. Missing effort or uncertain identities stop relevant comparisons for manual interpretation in s6.
Use native forms and formulas first. The calculation saving assumes manual summary preparation today; existing automatic summaries earn no additional saving.
No public map, external send or independent machine species identification is proposed.
research_questions: Can summaries retain uncertain observations and prevent invalid comparisons across unequal effort?

incremental.description: Maintain survey fields and test summary formulas.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 manual-summary scenario: B=100, R=85.5, gross=14.5; upkeep=4 gives central net=10.5. Field observation remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep public education, field observation and emergency response human while improving supporting records.
reach: Connect school requirements, park staff agreements and ecological observations.
role.ambitious_version: A park naturalist who prepares clear teaching material and traceable ecological records while remaining present with visitors and the park.
